sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Autofurnish Limited, BSE 544767, symbol AFLTD, ISIN INE18HI01019, BSE SME. Research cutoff 20 October 2026, information dates respected; records retrieved 21 October are used only for disclosures available by the cutoff. Closing reference 19 October ₹120.49 is a dated secondary observation, not an executable quote. Exchange interoperability master verifies 13,515,508 issued shares and 3000-share lot, not an NSE listing. Market cap ₹162.8484 cr. Horizon approximately five years to October 2031; nominal INR equity hurdle 15% before investor taxes, distinct from 14–18% assumed WACC. Illustrative liquidity reference ₹5 lakh is not a suitable-position recommendation. [M1–M4]

Scope is consolidated historical parent plus Golden Mace; FY26 uses Indian GAAP / Accounting Standards, not Ind AS. Golden Mace became 100% owned in March 2025. Chhariot 55% was acquired after March and is economically part of the cutoff group, but complete financials / consideration are unavailable. The forecast therefore clearly separates a conditional existing-business model from an unsupported full-group value. No credit for 100% of acquired earnings and no offsetting unidentified minority assets. [S1, S2, S3, S4]

G1 Conditional; G2 Hold—unresolved; G3 Conditional; G4 Conditional. G2 alone prevents favorable investment classification and IAS. There is no evidenced G1 fraud or G3 default override. High confidence in transcription of signed revised annual tables, lot and share count; Medium on reported financial history and known business mechanics; Low on asset realization, comparable organic growth, acquisition claims, actual cutoff cash and full-window liquidity. Overall conclusion confidence is Low on investability, not an average of better-supported observations. Detailed gate register below carries the precise resolution evidence.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV NS, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 4; IAS factors R NS, D 3, P 2, L NS. Scores are integer judgments, each supported by two facts and a contrary observation in the factor audit. Historical factors never exceed 8 at Medium confidence. REV is not scored from a 54.45% restart / perimeter-distorted CAGR. CAP and BAL are not filled with neutral 5 or weak 3 merely because material information is missing. [E1–E10]

BQS exact known contributions:0.20×4+0.20×3+0.10×5+0.10×2+0.08×5=2.50; missing REV / CAP/BAL weight 0.32. Coverage 68%; mathematical bound [2.82,5.70]; raw / final NS. GQS:0.20×5+0.15×4+0.10×2=1.80; missing REV / CAP weight 0.55; coverage 45%; raw bound [2.35,7.30]. Persistent CASH 2 invokes the explicit cap 5, giving cap-adjusted bound [2.35,5.00], but final remains NS, not 5. IAS known 0.20×3+0.10×2=0.80; Q (final BQS), R, L missing 0.70; coverage 30%; canonical mathematical bound [1.50,7.80], raw / final NS. Incorporating the BQS bound narrows only the informational IAS bound to [1.955,6.725]; it is not a point score or rank. G2 hold independently excludes investment ranking.

No weights are redistributed. All arithmetic uses Decimal; complete aggregates would display half-up to one decimal while classification uses unrounded numbers. GOV±1 shifts BQS bounds±0.20; EXEC±1 shifts±0.08, jointly±0.28. No governance cap 3 or funding cap 3 is applied because neither severe gate failure is evidenced. No extra discretionary risk haircut is added. The conditional core base spread would mechanically map to R1, but it is not a supported full-group R score. All three rankings remain ineligible, with the universe rankings provisional until research is complete.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
Incorporated 5 May 2015, the company manufactures and trades automotive accessories. Manufactured lines include body covers, floor mats, seat covers and organizers; traded lines include other vehicle accessories, lights / electronics and parts. Buyers choose fit, price, availability and styling; standard items can be substituted. Parent sales are principally B2B; Golden Mace adds online / B2C access. Revenue is recognized on transfer of risks / rewards and delivery, net of returns / discounts. Sales recorded are not equivalent to collections: FY26 receivables grew by ₹5.2519 cr. [S1 accounting notes; S2 pp 145–164,237–240]

The business history is essential. A 2021 business-transfer / commercial arrangement involving Scale Luxura and Upscalio was followed by low-demand / commercial disruption. Own manufacturing stopped November 2022 through March 2024; outsourcing under the Sahaprut arrangement and sale of old finished inventory continued. A June 2023 settlement and March 2024 outsourcing termination preceded the April 2024 restart. FY24 manufactured-goods sales included earlier inventory, not current production. This is not eleven uninterrupted years of comparable manufacturing growth. [S2 pp 19–34,145–164]

The prospectus separates FY25 manufactured-goods sales ₹24.3355 cr, traded-goods ₹8.7186 cr and webportal support ₹0.3060 cr. The annual comparative classifies approximately ₹0.3060 cr in other income, so annual sales ₹33.0541 cr and restated sales ₹33.3601 cr have the same total income. FY26 lacks that complete product / service split. 9M December 2025 restated revenue ₹28.2933 cr includes ₹0.60 cr support services; this is not annualized. Current order backlog, recurring-customer cohorts, realized ASPs and credit sales by customer are ND. Domestic vehicle demand provides context, not a verified market-share denominator. [S2 p 249; S1 PDF77,89]

sections.title: 5. Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
Proposed advantages need mechanisms, not labels. Brand / catalog and model-specific fitment can lower customer search costs, but no verified premium, repeat-purchase rate or protection against competing marketplace products is available. Manufacturing can improve assortment and lead times, yet the prospectus acknowledges competition without major entry barriers. Supplier relationships give procurement access but not proven exclusivity. The Auto / Mototrance brand history, trademark objection / reply and missing historical proprietorship-transfer deed limit confidence in legal brand protection; do not assume registrations are final. [S2 risk factors and business]

Customer concentration improved: largest customer 69.90%,43.79%,18.45%,14.07% in FY23, FY24, FY25,9M Dec 25; top 10 were 95.59%,94.22%,66.78%,48.84%. That is a real diversification signal, but anonymized counterparties and no confirmations prevent verification of connectedness or repeat economics. Suppliers remain concentrated: largest 11.34%,37.10%,45.31%,24.47%; top 10: 65.96%,85.67%,80.67%,54.32% over the same periods. A supplier failure can force more expensive sourcing or inventory buildup; a customer loss can slow collections and capacity utilization together. [S2 pp 19–34,145–164]

The prospectus itself identifies no exact listed peer. Three economically useful, non-identical comparators are used qualitatively. Elegant Auto Accessories offers closely overlapping seat covers / mats through dealers and end customers; private financials are unavailable and no premium multiple is inferred. Fiem manufactures technical automotive lighting / mirrors with OEM validation and aftermarket dealers, a stronger engineering / qualification mechanism but much more OEM exposure. Uno Minda’s diversified components, engineering and distribution illustrate the scale of technical and channel investment behind a broader franchise, not a multiple Autofurnish automatically deserves. No same-date peer P/E table is invented, and a broad auto-ancillary industry average in the prospectus is not intrinsic value. [S2 p 119, P1, P2, P3]

MOAT 3 reflects readily contestable economics. A capable entrant needs sourcing, catalogs, fulfillment and quality control, but a precise entry time / cost is ND. The evidence does not establish a network effect, entrenched switching barrier or defensible market-share leadership.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
Reported consolidated sales in ₹cr:FY23 ₹10.5886; FY24 ₹15.9100; FY25 annual ₹33.0541; FY26 ₹39.0120. Annual additions ₹5.3214 cr, ₹17.1441 cr, ₹5.9579 cr; FY25 restated alternative ₹33.3601 cr is retained separately. FY26 growth against its own annual comparative 18.02%; against the unreclassified prospectus number 16.94%, a presentation mismatch not a new economic growth statistic. FY23–26 reported CAGR 54.45% uses three actual intervals. 5Y/10Y CAGR is ND because six / eleven comparable annual observations are not available. The issuer’s FY22 file actually contains Golden Mace accounts and is not substituted for parent history. [S1 PDF76–78, S2 pp 232–234, S8]

The driver bridge is partly observable: FY24 includes Golden Mace consolidation, manufacturing restart drives FY25, manufactured / traded mix changes materially, and FY25 support-service revenue is reclassified in the annual. Volume, realized price / mix, returns and constant-scope acquisition contribution are not fully quantified. Therefore the 54.45% CAGR cannot be called organic market-share gains, while the 18.02% latest year is genuine reported commercial growth but not sufficient to repair the three-year base. Latest comparable TTM is FY26; no verified September 2026 results by cutoff. 9M December 2025 sales ₹28.2933 cr and CFO−₹4.3485 cr are historical offer-document context, not a post-IPO trajectory. [S2 pp 234,249]

Economic cross-check: material value added, defined as sales less material consumed, traded purchases and inventory movement, is ₹8.2961 cr in FY25 annual and ₹9.7625 cr in FY26, roughly 25.1% and 25.0% of sales. It excludes employee, processing and selling allocations and is not fully allocated gross profit. This supports some real value addition rather than pure pass-through, but does not establish unit-volume growth or durable excess margin. REV remains NS under the explicit rule for materially obscured underlying demand.

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Management disclosed annual installed capacity 18,80,100 pieces, FY25 utilization 13,84,380 pieces/73.63%, and 9M December 2025 utilization 16,24,440 pieces/86.4% of stated annual capacity. The latter denominator / period ambiguity is retained; it is not multiplied into an annual utilization forecast. A January 2026 engineer certificate supports stated machinery capacity, not demand, yields, pricing or cash realization. IPO plans ₹1.889 cr machinery and ₹9.30 cr working capital, but purchase-order / commissioning and actual proceeds-use verification remain missing. [S2 pp 101–115,145–164]

A defensible bottom-up model cannot convert mixed covers, mats, organizers and traded goods into a single ASP without a product volume bridge. Instead, the reproducible cash-constrained existing-business path is explicitly conditional: common modeled October 2026 run-rate sales ₹40.36 cr; base 6% growth gives terminal ₹54.01 cr; bear 3%₹46.79 cr; bull 12%₹71.13 cr. Base maintains the closing operating-capital intensity, initially ₹30.3323 cr or 77.75% of FY26 sales. Initial machinery spend is funded from the IPO earmark; thereafter each ₹5 of incremental annual sales requires ₹1 growth capex, with ₹3 sensitivity; maintenance 0.27656 cr / year is an analyst estimate, not a claim that depreciation equals maintenance. Bull requires an 8 percentage-point sales reduction in operating-capital intensity over three years, not instant free cash. [E4, E6]

These assumptions make explicit why a large market is insufficient. At unchanged working-capital intensity,12% core growth produces a ₹4.78 cr peak post-entry funding gap; 22% produces ₹33.35 cr. Neither gets an ordinary-case IRR or imaginary debt / equity rescue. The base slows growth because cash supply is finite, not because a lower growth rate is called management guidance. Capacity / productivity and sell-through must ultimately validate this path.

GQS is NS; the known cash evidence caps any otherwise computable GQS at 5. Capitalization needs include working capital, not just modest visible PPE. A stable-growth reinvestment identity is only a cross-check here: the latest 4.77% incremental accounting proxy does not support fast self-funded compounding. Chhariot had nil historical turnover; the EV runway is unproven and receives no sales / value credit merely because the sector can grow.

sections.title: 8. Management Governance and Execution
sections.text:
Puneet Arora and Ruppal Wadhwa are the key promoter-directors. Prospectus post-issue promoter shares imply 68.57% if unchanged; an independently verified September ownership / encumbrance filing was not obtained. High ownership is not minority protection by itself. FY26 direct remuneration ₹0.36 cr each, plus ₹0.12 cr each for two relatives, totals ₹0.96 cr or 26.42% of group PAT, unchanged on the disclosed comparative. Outstanding family remuneration ₹0.662843 cr sits within employee payables ₹0.843333 cr; it is not subtracted twice in the model. Related-party loan receivable ₹0.3224 cr remains unchanged; director loan ₹0.167595 cr is included in debt. [S1 PDF91–93, S2 shareholding]

M A N V & Associates succeeded Kapoor Batra after the earlier term ended; prospectus appointment period April 2024–March 2029 is not evidence of a scope-driven resignation. The financial audit opinion is unmodified. Separately, the auditor reports absent software audit-trail functionality, and the group note says management supplied no confirmations for debtors, creditors and supplier advances. These are material reliability concerns but not proof of fabricated accounts. The reported internal-control exemption / listing-timing explanation is preserved without making an independent legal-compliance judgment. Golden Mace’s old statutory-dues item of ₹2600 is not exaggerated into a major group default. [S1 PDF70–75,93,100; S2 p 79]

The 4 September acquisition is reported completed, not merely proposed:55% Chhariot EMob for cash at face value, remaining 45% with promoters; historical turnover nil. Two secondary reports corroborate completion. The absolute consideration, acquired debt / cash, shareholder rights, guarantees and loan terms are not verified. A loan up to ₹2.5 cr was approved, not proven disbursed. Conflicting related-party language in the reported filings requires the originals, not a conclusion of wrongdoing. The model reserves the entire ₹2.5 cr and credits no EV value; it does not pretend the acquisition disappeared. [S3, S4]

Dated legal disclosure: the May 2026 prospectus reports Aeroids Corporation’s cheque complaint against Ruppal Wadhwa, claimed ₹6,38,508. The response disputes quality and says the cheque was security; the matter was pending complainant evidence, next date 31 July 2026 as then disclosed. No conviction or verified October outcome is claimed. Autofurnish’s own complaint against Oruga for ₹1,07,994 was also pending. Pre-IPO filing errors / corrections and missing historical transfer documentation are described as disclosed, with no issuer-reported show-cause / fine at prospectus date. [S2 pp 289–290, risk factors]

Promises-versus-delivery: April 2024 manufacturing restart is delivered; March 2025 Golden Mace 100% ownership delivered; May 2026 fresh IPO / listing delivered; FY27 machinery deployment and collection improvement not yet verified; September Chhariot control delivered per secondary sources but operating turnover / cash returns unproven; September 21₹17.9 lakh machinery-loan approval is not assumed funded. EXEC 5 reflects mixed adaptation and delivery, not a penalty for missing promotional forecasts.

sections.text:
Observed market cap ₹162.8484 cr is based on current issued shares, not historical EPS shares. FY26 reported P/E 44.82 x; conservative PAT excluding all other income at 27% tax gives 57.58 x. March pre-IPO claims produce stale EV ₹175.12 cr, EV/EBITDA 31.76 x and EV/sales 4.49 x; these are date-mismatched diagnostics, not current EV. Pre-IPO book P/B 8.88 x; adding net IPO only gives proforma 5.17 x before later profits / deployment. Current unrestricted cash and Chhariot NCI / senior claims are unknown. Negative FCF proxy gives no positive owner-yield argument. [E4, M1, M2]

The linked model starts from actual 31 March balances, then a common unobserved April–October stub with 6% annualized sales growth/12.5% EBIT margin. It is not reported October cash. May gross IPO ₹14.6001 cr less unpaid cost ₹1.34485 cr adds ₹13.25525 cr; ₹0.10515 cr expense was already prepaid, so it is not paid twice. WC ₹9.30 cr, machinery ₹1.889 cr and GCP ₹1.9611 cr remain restricted until eligible core spending. Expenditure releases restrictions but is not a second cash cost. Full ₹2.5 cr EV loan commitment is treated unavailable in September, purchase consideration is an explicit unknown parameter (default zero only for diagnostics, ₹1 crore tested), and no EV revenue / recovery is credited. Opening tax, statutory / employee balances, debt, interest and benefit obligations each enter once through ONWC, payments or terminal claims. [S1, S2, E6, claims register]

Five-year periods are November 2026–October 2031, approximately five years from 19 October entry (no dividends). Bear:3% growth,10% EBIT, receivables+15 days / inventory+15 days,6 x terminal EV/EBIT; terminal sales ₹46.79 cr, terminal price ₹20.88, conditional IRR-29.57%, price change-82.67%. Base:6%,12.5%, no working-capital improvement,10 x; sales ₹54.01 cr, terminal price ₹51.71, IRR-15.56%. Bull:12%,14.5%,8 percentage points of working-capital intensity improvement over 36 months,12 x; sales ₹71.13 cr, terminal price ₹91.29, IRR-5.40%. All are conditional core diagnostics, not full-group target prices or canonical R. They assume modeled October free cash ₹7.50 cr, no hidden acquired obligations, no additional equity / dilution, and specified debt maturities. Post-entry fundability is tested separately from unobserved pre-entry buffer deficits; no invented historical rescue is inserted. [E6]

Base terminal EV ₹67.51 cr less debt / benefit claims ₹5.28 cr plus surplus cash ₹7.65 cr gives equity ₹69.89 cr, divided by 1.3515508 crore shares. Rent stays in EBIT under AS accounts; no duplicate Ind AS lease debt is introduced. Remaining OD / director debt is deducted; related loan asset recovery is zero. For the acquired 55% venture, no 100% earnings or hidden NCI value is added.

The model supplies annual cash bridges and a 5×5 growth / exit multiple grid. 12% growth without WC reform needs ₹4.78 cr and 22% needs ₹33.35 cr additional cash; IRR null in both. Changing terminal multiple cannot finance an earlier deficit. Other tested cases include full OD recall,1 crore unknown consideration,3 crore pre-entry cash leakage, family-payable unwind, capex turnover 3 x and term coupon 18%. At the base operating path,15% hurdle requires 48.16 x terminal EV/EBIT rather than 10 x. Conditional hurdle entry prices at 12%/15%/18% are ₹29.34/₹25.71/₹22.60, not observable fair values or trade instructions, and not sufficient to clear G2. Five percent entry / exit execution friction reduces base IRR further to-17.24%; actual spread / impact ND. R / IAS remain NS.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
sections.text:
The critical variable is cash realization of working-capital assets, not the next announced product. Customer loss or poor sell-through can simultaneously reduce utilization / margins, age receivables and strand inventory. Bank debt and tax / employee claims then compete with machinery and EV funding; an equity raise at a weak price can destroy per-share value even if consolidated revenue keeps growing. At the observed P/E, ordinary multiple normalization creates substantial loss without any fraud or insolvency. [S1, S2, E4, E6]

The strongest credible downside is a cash-starved, low-barrier distributor / manufacturer with a speculative related-party diversification. The conditional core bear loses 82.67% of quote value and still ends with positive equity; unknown acquired claims could worsen recovery. The strongest counterargument is that IPO cash absorbs the investment phase, new inventory sells, customer diversification continues and machinery raises productivity. This is not dismissed: the restrained essential-operation stress (sales−15%, EBIT 10%, receivable+30 days, inventory+15 days, no further growth, full EV cash use) remains funded in the modeled post-entry period. Thus discretionary 22% unfunded growth is not misrepresented as inevitable corporate failure. [E6]

Recovery is not automatically supported by book equity. Receivables and inventory ₹33.4087 cr dominate March assets ₹36.6524 cr; their unconfirmed realization and potential markdowns matter more than a low nominal face value or IPO price. The completed EV company’s debt, guarantees and minority terms could alter priority and cash access. March asset haircuts cannot establish a current floor without post-IPO cash and transaction records. Impairment risk is High, not a numerical probability. Falsification requires independent receipts, stock realization and a fully reconciled acquired / parent cash ledger. A normal quoted drawdown is not the same as evidence of default, and unresolved evidence is not an allegation-as-conviction.

sections.title: 12. Five Times and Ten Times Feasibility
sections.text:
A multibagger claim is speculative / unsupported on available evidence. Fivefold price growth over five years requires 37.97% annualized; tenfold requires 58.49%. Business revenue growth is not equivalent to equity or per-share growth. Current-share FY26 EPS is ₹2.6883; even ignoring dividends, a 5×price at a normalized 15 x P/E would require terminal EPS ₹40.16, about 14.94×current earnings per share; 10×requires ₹80.33, about 29.88×. These imply roughly 71.7% and 97.3% annualized EPS growth, before adverse dilution, on a base where cash realization is negative. Those are feasibility arithmetic, not forecasts. [E4, M1, M2]

No verified product-volume, accessible-share, manufacturing-capacity and funding bridge supports that scale. The 12% growth-without-reform and 22% expansion tests already require additional capital. EV participation does not fill the gap when the acquired entity has nil historical turnover and missing obligations. A successful new business could change the outcome, but it would need independently funded unit economics, disclosed ownership claims and attributable cash profits, not a sector TAM multiple. The compounder designation is not met.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The following research checks are specific to Autofurnish. An operating warning triggers investigation, while documented severe governance or essential-funding failure changes a gate. Price movements alone do not resolve evidence gaps. No reminder or recurring monitoring automation has been created. [E1–E9]

1. Receivable confirmations and collections. Baseline: ₹16.0152 crore at March 2026, closing receivable days 149.8, and note 35 missing confirmations. Obtain independent confirmations and receipts against both aged and incremental balances. Investigate persistent days above 150 with slowing sales. Material unrecoverable or false balances would break the cash-realization thesis. Review with the next results and before any upgrade.

2. Inventory realization. Baseline: ₹17.3935 crore, up 80.18%, without an adequate age/markdown schedule. Require SKU ageing, sell-through and cash collection without major write-offs. Investigate inventory days above the FY26 material-cost proxy of 169 without corresponding sales. Material stranded stock or funding impairment is a thesis break. Review with the next half-year statement and stock audit.

3. Cash after interest. Baseline: FY26 CFO −₹5.7415 crore, with an additional ₹1.3640 crore of interest in financing cash flow. Require sustained positive cash after interest at restrained growth. Another profitable period with major negative CFO is a warning; essential payments dependent on an uncommitted rescue would change G3. Review every cash-flow report.

4. IPO deployment. Baseline: gross ₹14.6001 crore; objects include ₹9.30 crore working capital, ₹1.889 crore machinery and ₹1.9611 crore general corporate purposes. Reconcile bank balances, earmarked funds, utilization and issue expenses. Unreconciled or non-object uses require investigation; evidenced material unauthorized diversion would change G1. Review the next utilization filing.

5. Chhariot obligations and minority terms. Baseline: completed 55% acquisition reported, promoters 45%, approved loan up to ₹2.5 crore, absolute purchase consideration ND. Require the agreement, opening balance sheet, loans, guarantees, rights and consolidation. More cash commitments without sales/unit economics are a warning; unbounded parent obligations or evidenced minority harm could break the thesis. Review the next transaction filing.

6. Capacity and orders. Baseline: ₹1.889 crore IPO machinery planned, commissioning not verified. Seek invoices, commissioning, product qualification and cash-paying demand. Investigate FY27 delays without a demand/funding explanation. Stranded capital alongside worsening core cash would invalidate the expansion thesis.

7. Debt maturities and facilities. Baseline: March debt ₹12.7925 crore, current term maturities ₹1.8591 crore and overdraft ₹4.9941 crore. Verify actual residual EMIs, facility availability and covenants. Rising debt faster than cash profit or higher overdue charges are warnings. Verified default or an essential unfinanceable payment would change G3. Review each results and material disclosure.

8. Governance and litigation. Baseline: unmodified opinion, absent software audit trail, note 35 and the pending case disclosed in the May prospectus. Seek control remediation, confirmations, RPT terms and current case status. Repeated errors or withheld material information are warnings, not automatically fraud. Substantiated serious diversion/manipulation/minority abuse would change G1.

9. Tradeability. Baseline: 3,000-share lot and 58 of 60 observed sessions, with 5 August/14 October missing. Require complete official turnover and executable depth. Falling median activity or one-sided circuits are warnings. Suspension or effective inability to exit changes G4. The November lot change is not effective at cutoff. Check before implementation for the actual lot-sized position.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold—unresolved; financing-sensitive post-restart accessory business with unproven diversification. Research priority High because the unanswered items are consequential, not because return potential is demonstrated. BQS, GQS, IAS are NS; no numeric matrix cell or universal rank is forced. Not an evidence-backed compounder: moat 3, cash 2 and critical missing REV / CAP/BAL prevent the required quality conditions even before valuation. G2 hold disallows favorable investment classification. [E1–E9]

The quote also looks demanding under the disclosed core diagnostics, but the main conclusion is not simply “wait for a lower price.” Before investment consideration, obtain independent working-capital confirmations / receipts, a current cash / use-of-proceeds bridge, actual repayment availability, and the full completed acquisition agreement and acquired balance sheet. A valid lower entry case must still be funded and include all shareholder claims. If these records establish serious misconduct, G1 may fail; if credible essential operations are demonstrated unfinanceable, G3 may fail. Neither is asserted today. If the user already owns it, position size, tax basis and actual lot liquidity would be needed for an execution-aware review; no holding or exit instruction is invented.
